mainEntity.name: How much does a car depreciate in five years?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common rule of thumb is around 40% to 60% for a new car, depending on the model. This calculator's typical curve loses about 50% over five years for a midsize SUV, but individual vehicles vary widely.

mainEntity.name: Which cars hold their value best?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trucks and some popular SUVs tend to keep more value, while luxury sedans and many electric vehicles have lost more. Reliability, fuel prices, incentives and new model launches all move the market.

mainEntity.name: Is it cheaper to buy used?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, because the first owner pays for the steepest depreciation. Use the condition setting to see the effect, but include the cost of any extra maintenance an older car needs.
Yes. Higher mileage lowers resale value and can accelerate wear. This tool uses your mileage to work out cost per mile; for a precise resale value, compare listings with similar mileage.

mainEntity.name: What is total cost of ownership?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is everything that leaving the car in your driveway costs over the time you own it: the value it loses, loan interest, insurance, maintenance, fuel and other running costs, less nothing you get back except the resale value.
